key_insight: UPEBNL makes causal Bayesian network learning scalable, allowing interpretable cancer prescreening models to be built from large electronic health record datasets.
clinical_relevance: The approach may help clinicians and researchers understand risk pathways for esophageal and colorectal cancer while supporting more transparent prescreening decisions.
method: Adaptive data slicing to split large EHR data for parallel learning
Quality-aware structure aggregation to combine learned subnetworks
Global directed acyclic graph construction for stable causal-interpretable models
evidence_signal: In simulations, the framework improved structural recovery by nearly 40% and sped up conventional CBN learning by up to 221.28-fold; in EHR prescreening it achieved AUC 0.8171 for esophageal cancer and 0.784 for colorectal cancer.
watch_item: Like other observational EHR-based models, the learned causal directions may still reflect data quality and confounding rather than confirmed biological causality.
paper_title: Scalable Causal-Interpretable Machine Learning for Cancer Prescreening Using Electronic Health Records
